hip_knee:K7.title: K7 · Fast swelling after a twist, or the kneecap popped out
hip_knee:K7.sourceText:
K7 · Fast swelling after a twist, or the kneecap popped out
ASK: Did you hear or feel a pop? How fast did it swell? Did the kneecap slide out to the side?
POSITIVE IF: the knee swelled within the first few hours — that means bleeding inside the joint, typical of a ligament tear (ACL), a fracture or a kneecap dislocation.
NOTE: this does NOT rule out exercise. ACL tears can be managed rehab-first (KANON trial, Frobell 2010). A first-time kneecap dislocation needs an X-ray to look for a broken-off fragment of bone or cartilage (BOAST 2024).
WHO: anyone trained

hip_knee:K7Y.sourceText:
SOON — WITHIN ABOUT A WEEK
Make sure K1 (fracture) is cleared. Refer for a ligament exam within about a week; first kneecap dislocation → X-ray. Start gentle bending and straightening and thigh-muscle tightening now.
Then continue down this list, and in Stage 2 take the “specific injury” branch (KQ2).

hip_knee:K8.title: K8 · Child or teen: a HIP problem showing up as knee pain
hip_knee:K8.sourceText:
K8 · Child or teen: a HIP problem showing up as knee pain
ASK: An older child or teenager with a limp and knee or thigh pain? A younger child who won’t stand on the leg? Pain in the groin or thigh as well? Fever?
CHECK: lying down, bend the hip to 90° — does the leg swing outward by itself (Drehmann sign)? Turn the hip inward — limited or painful compared with the other side? The knee itself often looks normal — that is the clue.
EVIDENCE: a slipped capital femoral epiphysis (the ball of the hip slips at the growth plate) shows up as knee or thigh pain alone in about 15% of cases and is often missed (Peck 2017). In a feverish child who won’t bear weight, 2 of the 4 Kocher criteria are already present — about a 40% chance of hip infection (Kocher 1999).
WHO: physio-level (hip rotation); anyone trained (history)
RULE: every child with knee pain gets a hip exam. Any sign present?

hip_knee:K8Y.title: EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
hip_knee:K8Y.sourceText:

No weight-bearing (crutches), orthopaedics and a hip X-ray today.

hip_knee:K9.title: K9 · Possible tumour or serious bone disease
hip_knee:K9.sourceText:
K9 · Possible tumour or serious bone disease
ASK: Constant pain that no rest or position eases? Waking at night with it? History of cancer? Unexplained weight loss? A lump? A teenager with deep bone pain around the knee?
CHECK: compare both thighs and shins; feel for a firm swelling that is not the joint itself.
NOTE: night pain ALONE is common in knee osteoarthritis. Escalate when night pain comes WITH constant pain, weight loss, a cancer history or a lump. Around the knee, bone tumours also occur in teenagers.
TEAM DATA: in the NAS records, night-pain patients were referred less often than average (4.7% vs 8.7%) — this check exists to fix that.
WHO: anyone trained

hip_knee:K10.title: K10 · Whole-body (inflammatory) or post-viral arthritis
hip_knee:K10.sourceText:
K10 · Whole-body (inflammatory) or post-viral arthritis
ASK: Morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes that eases with movement? Swelling in 3 or more joints, or in the hands, wrists or feet? A high fever with rash before the joint pain (chikungunya, dengue)? Psoriasis (scaly skin rash), bowel disease, a red painful eye, or diarrhoea or a urine infection in the last month? Back pain that improves with exercise and is worse with rest?
CHECK: count swollen joints — both hands, wrists, knees, ankles and feet.
POSITIVE IF: 3 or more swollen joints, or any swelling of small joints.
EVIDENCE: about 25% of people with chikungunya develop long-lasting inflammatory joint disease (27% in Indian studies) (Rodriguez-Morales 2016).
WHO: anyone trained

hip_knee:K11.title: K11 · Possible tuberculosis (TB) of the knee
hip_knee:K11.sourceText:
K11 · Possible tuberculosis (TB) of the knee
ASK: One knee swollen for weeks to months? Night sweats, cough, weight loss, TB in the family or past TB? HIV or diabetes?
CHECK: compare thigh size (muscle wasting); feel for a soft, thick, “boggy” swelling.
NOTE: after the spine, the hip and knee are the commonest joints for TB, mostly in younger people in TB-endemic areas (osteoarticular TB review, 2020).

hip_knee:K12.title: K12 · Pain coming from the back or the hip (referred pain)
hip_knee:K12.sourceText:
K12 · Pain coming from the back or the hip (referred pain)
ASK: Does the pain start in the back or buttock and spread past the knee? Numbness, tingling or weakness in the foot? NEW trouble controlling the bladder or bowel, or numbness between the legs (the “saddle” area)?
CHECK: do squatting and bending/straightening the knee change the pain? Then: bend and arch the back; straight-leg raise; turn the hip in and out with it bent to 90°.
POSITIVE IF: knee movements don’t change the pain, but back or hip movements reproduce it.
NOTE: hip osteoarthritis commonly refers pain to the front and inside of the knee.

hip_knee:n5_169.title: SAFETY MODIFIERS — not stops; they change who signs off and how hard you start
hip_knee:n5_169.sourceText:
SAFETY MODIFIERS — not stops; they change who signs off and how hard you start
• Chest pain, breathlessness or fainting with effort → doctor before progressive exercise.
• Blood pressure clearly uncontrolled → doctor sign-off first (use the local cut-off).
• Diabetes → check feet and skin before kneeling or barefoot work.
• Pregnancy → avoid lying flat on the back after the first trimester.

CONTEXT TO RECORD (changes the plan)
• Underweight is common here (median BMI 18.8 in the NAS data), so standard “lose weight” advice often doesn’t apply.
• Floor sitting, squatting toilets, kneeling for prayer, field work and carrying water define the goals.
• Fear that exercise will damage the knee, low mood and poor sleep slow recovery — address them in education.

hip_knee:n3_9.title: HOW TO USE THIS BOARD
hip_knee:n3_9.sourceText:
HOW TO USE THIS BOARD
1. Start at the black START box and follow the arrows.
2. Yellow boxes are QUESTIONS. Ask them in plain words, pick the white answer box that matches what the patient says, and follow its arrow.
3. Blue boxes are HANDS-ON CHECKS. Each one says what to do, what counts as positive, how accurate it is, and who can usually do it.
4. Every pathway runs in 3 stages: Stage 1 safety screen (is this safe to treat with exercise?) → Stage 2 working diagnosis (which problem is it?) → Stage 3 baseline and plan (measure, set the exercise dose, re-test).
5. Dashed grey arrows jump to another part of the board. Box codes (e.g. K3, HT2, KD8) let you jump by name.

Starting assumption: non-musculoskeletal causes (heart, abdomen, skin, etc.) have already been ruled out.

hip_knee:n3_13.title: HOW TO READ THE ACCURACY NUMBERS
hip_knee:n3_13.sourceText:
HOW TO READ THE ACCURACY NUMBERS
Sensitivity — out of 100 people who really HAVE the problem, how many the test catches. A highly sensitive test that comes back NEGATIVE helps rule the problem OUT.
Specificity — out of 100 people who do NOT have it, how many the test correctly clears. A highly specific test that comes back POSITIVE helps rule the problem IN.
Positive predictive value — of the people who test positive, how many actually have it.
Likelihood ratio (LR) — how strongly a result shifts the odds. LR+ above 10 = strong rule-in; LR− below 0.1 = strong rule-out.
Cluster — several findings counted together; beats any single test for almost every condition here.
Consensus — expert agreement only; no accuracy study was found. Treat these boxes with more caution.
Working diagnosis — the best label you can act on without imaging. It is confirmed, or revised, by how the patient responds at the week-4 re-test.

hip_knee:n3_17.title: PLAIN-LANGUAGE GLOSSARY
hip_knee:n3_17.sourceText:
PLAIN-LANGUAGE GLOSSARY
Flexion / extension — bending / straightening a joint.
Internal / external rotation — turning the thigh or shin inward / outward.
Adduction / abduction — moving the leg toward / away from the middle of the body.
Medial / lateral — inner side / outer side. Anterior / posterior — front / back.
Effusion — swelling (fluid) inside the joint.
Weight-bearing — standing or walking on the leg.
Isometric exercise — the muscle tightens and holds without the joint moving; usually the least painful way to start loading.
Irritability — how easily the pain flares up and how long it takes to settle.
Referred pain — pain felt in one place but coming from another (e.g. a hip problem felt at the knee).
Imaging — X-ray, ultrasound or MRI scan.
Doctor — the medical officer on the team. Orthopaedics — bone and joint specialists.
Osteoarthritis (OA) — "wear and repair" changes in a joint's cartilage and bone.

hip_knee:n3_21.title: WHO CAN DO EACH CHECK (guidance, never a stop)
hip_knee:n3_21.sourceText:
WHO CAN DO EACH CHECK (guidance, never a stop)
Anyone trained — a health worker after short training: questions, looking, pressing, simple movements.
Basic kit — needs a thermometer, tape measure, blood-pressure cuff or phone app.
Physio-level — needs a physiotherapist's or doctor's hands-on skill; can be done by video review or at referral.
If nobody with the skill is available: record the history, film the movement, note the test as "not done" and keep going — the pathway still works, with a little less certainty.

amendments.issue: Hip/knee START assumes non-musculoskeletal causes were already excluded; the spine START says the pain only 'seems' musculoskeletal. Neither says who established this or how.
amendments.proposal: Ask who established musculoskeletal eligibility and on what basis before Stage 1. 'Unclear' does not pass automatically: safety screening and history capture continue, but safety clearance, candidate release and any exercise plan stay blocked until a reviewer resolves it.

amendments.issue: Both boards say to note a skilled test as 'not done' and keep going ('never a stop').
amendments.proposal: Record not_performed with a reason and who lacked the skill. Continue history capture. Never treat it as negative: the dependent diagnosis is not produced, safety clearance stays incomplete, and the plan is blocked until someone with the capability performs the test or a clinician records a decision.
amendments.implementedAs: engine: answer status not_performed; capability check on safety checks and exams; blockers SAFETY_INCOMPLETE / EXAM_PENDING

amendments.issue: PASS boxes label the problem 'EXERCISE-RESPONSIVE (BY EXCLUSION)' and say the label is 'confirmed' by improvement at week 4.
amendments.proposal: Display 'No listed safety concern reported on this screen' with the source wording kept in the provenance view. Never state that a diagnosis is confirmed by a negative screen or by week-4 improvement; improvement is recorded as a response, and the working assessment stays a clinician decision.
amendments.implementedAs: ui wording keys safety.cleared_*; engine never sets 'confirmed' automatically

amendments.proposal: Use the 22 connectors as the diagnosis-to-group mapping (they agree with the group text). Treat the add-on module as a measurement module, not an exercise list. Diagnoses with no arrow get no proposed group (clinician decides). KD5/KD16 carry a doctor-clearance precaution from E2.
amendments.implementedAs: compile: node.exerciseGroups from connectors; plan: precaution E2_DOCTOR_CLEARANCE

amendments.issue: Outcome boxes mix referral timing, whether assessment continues, and exercise restriction in free text. Stage headers say 'Any YES stops the pathway'; K7Y says 'Then continue down this list'.
amendments.proposal: Keep three separate fields per outcome. Timing = source headline. Assessment continues only where the box says so (K7Y). Exercise restriction parsed from explicit phrases; otherwise a class default marked derived_default. Every raised outcome blocks the exercise plan until a clinician records a clearance decision.
amendments.implementedAs: compile: outcome policy; engine: alerts + blocker ALERT_UNRESOLVED

amendments.issue: SWITCH PATHWAY boxes bundle several actions (go to hip pathway, go to low-back pathway, emergency for bladder/bowel/saddle symptoms, 'assess and treat both', shoulder pathway that does not exist in the boards). Only K12Y has a connector (to the hip pathway); L11Y points to another board in text only.
amendments.proposal: Ask an explicit follow-up to pick the action. Bladder/bowel/saddle choice raises a same-day emergency. A pathway target opens a linked complaint that carries the origin; a pathway already in the origin chain is not re-entered (loop guard) and goes to clinician review. Unsupported targets (shoulder, non-MSK) become referral items.
amendments.implementedAs: overlay.switches; engine: switch step, linked complaints, loop guard

amendments.issue: Several answers say 'back to K10/H3/H5/H9/H11' with no connector; others have a connector back into a Stage 1 check (LT2c>L5, LT5b>L12, NT3d>N6). LT2c text says 'back to L1 / L5' but the arrow goes only to L5.
amendments.proposal: Stop routine progression, show which Stage 1 check(s) the source points to, and require the check to be re-answered or sent to clinician review. No diagnosis or plan is released from that branch. If the re-answered check is still denied while the contradicting answer stands, it stays in review.

amendments.issue: KT6b>KT7 and KT7b>KT6 form a loop with no exit; KN1 loops back to KT1 ('re-test in 1-2 weeks'); KT11 and KT12 only have a positive result box.
amendments.proposal: When a walk returns to a node it has already passed, stop and send to clinician review with the trace (no diagnosis). Offer 'negative / none of these' on single-result tests, which also goes to review because the source has no branch.
amendments.implementedAs: engine: halt CYCLE; exam option none_of_these -> halt NO_SOURCE_BRANCH

amendments.issue: KQ3 uses under 16 / 16-44 / 45+. HQ2 uses '50 or older (from 45 if the pattern is typical)', '16-49 and active', 'under 16' so ages 45-49 fit two answers and inactive adults under 45 fit none. KN2 routes by age in text but has a single arrow to KT5.
amendments.proposal: Never auto-answer from age. Flag a contradiction when the chosen answer cannot match the recorded age (HQ2a accepts 45+). KN2: age 45+ goes to KT5, younger to KT6 as the text says; unknown age goes to review.

amendments.issue: Dashed arrows run from urgent/soon outcomes to a diagnosis 'once confirmed stable' / 'after clearance' (L6Y>LD12, L9Y>LD4, N8Y>ND11, N10Y>ND11).
amendments.proposal: Do not follow these automatically. Show them to the reviewing clinician as a possible next step that requires documented medical clearance.
amendments.implementedAs: compile: outcome.gatedNext; review UI lists them

amendments.issue: Children are handled by single checks ('every child with knee pain gets a hip exam', physio-level) and a few branches. Exercise groups and doses are written for adults.
amendments.proposal: For patients under 18, require clinician review before any plan is released and show the paediatric checks as needing a skilled examination. Threshold 18 follows L9/N10 wording; KQ3 uses 16 for growth plates. Needs clinical decision.

amendments.issue: Safety modifiers ('doctor before progressive exercise', 'use the local cut-off' for blood pressure) have no numeric threshold and no branch.
amendments.proposal: Ask each modifier as a recorded history field. Any modifier present or unknown adds a clinician sign-off requirement to the plan. No blood-pressure cut-off is invented; the local value must be supplied by the programme.

amendments.issue: Accuracy figures, NAS statistics and citations are unverified. Named questionnaires (KOOS, WOMAC, IKDC, Kujala, VISA, HOOS, HAGOS, Roland-Morris, Oswestry, STarT Back, Örebro, NDI, PHQ-9...) have licence and translation requirements.
amendments.proposal: Show evidence lines only in the provenance view, labelled unverified. Never compute an individual probability. Do not reproduce questionnaire items; allow an externally obtained total to be recorded. Aggregate statements (e.g. median BMI) are never turned into individual advice.
amendments.implementedAs: ui: provenance view; measures type external_score

amendments.issue: Buttock pain is an entry to both the hip pathway and the low-back pathway on different boards.
amendments.proposal: Let the CHW choose either entry; both pathways screen for the other (H10, L11). Clinical decision needed on a preferred default.
amendments.implementedAs: ui: body location choices list buttock under both

amendments.issue: SOON outcomes allow gentle exercise per the colour key, but only K7Y states that the checklist continues.
amendments.proposal: Continue assessment only for K7Y. L9Y and N10Y stop routine progression pending doctor review. Exercise for all SOON outcomes needs clinician clearance in this build.
amendments.implementedAs: compile: assessmentMayContinue from source text only
